identity.name: Ya'rubid dynasty
alt_names: Imamate of Oman under the Ya'rubids

land.text: Oman under Ahmad bin Said, elected imam in 1744 and victorious over Bal'arab bin Himyar in the second half of 1749; Cliopatria's Sultanate of Oman shape of 1744 already includes the Swahili coast

successors.note: The Ya'rubids page ends the dynasty in 1742 in its text and the Omani Empire page in 1719; the Ahmad bin Said and Bal'arab bin Himyar pages end 'Yaruba power' with Bal'arab's defeat in 1749, which this dossier follows. Cliopatria's row ends in 1743.

capitals.name: Nizwa
capitals.note: Nasir bin Murshid moved the capital to Nizwa, the former Ibadhi Imamate capital, early in his reign from 1624 (paraphrase); the page does not date a later move before Saif bin Sultan's residence at Rustaq (1692).

capitals.name: Rustaq
capitals.note: Saif bin Sultan made the castle of Rustaq his residence during his rule (1692-1711).

capitals.name: Al-Hazm (near Rustaq)
capitals.note: Sultan bin Saif II set up his capital at Al-Hazm around 1710-1718; coordinates approximate.

capitals.name: Nizwa
capitals.note: Bal'arab bin Himyar, elected imam again in 1743, held the interior and was based at Nizwa. The seat in 1719-1742 is not given by the pages opened.

rulers.name: Nasir bin Murshid
rulers.note: Imams and reign years as the Ya'rubids page lists them; several reigns overlap or are broken, as the page gives them.

rulers.name: Bil'arab bin Sultan
rulers.note: Overlaps Sultan bin Saif's last years on the page.

rulers.name: Muhammad bin Nasir
rulers.note: Seized power in the civil war that began after the 1718 succession dispute.

rulers.name: Saif bin Sultan II
rulers.note: Fourth reign; overlaps Bal'arab bin Himyar's first reign on the page.

rulers.name: Bal'arab bin Himyar
rulers.note: First reign, 'holding power in the interior of Oman' (Bal'arab bin Himyar page).

rulers.name: Bal'arab bin Himyar
rulers.note: Second reign; defeated and killed by Ahmad bin Said in the second half of 1749.

correction.text: the imamate of Nasir bin Murshid in 1624-1625, located only by his capital Nizwa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Ya'rubid shape begins in 1626, the page dates the dynasty from 1624 ('rulers of Oman between 1624 and 1742'; Nasir bin Murshid, imam 1624-1649). The page names Nizwa as his capital, not a frontier.

correction.text: the 1626 shape without the Portuguese strongpoints at Julfar (to 1632), Sohar (to 1642) and Muscat (to 1649), which the ledger adds in 1633, 1643 and 1650

keyframe_review.note: 88,000 km2 over Oman and the United Arab Emirates for 1626-1652. The Portuguese still held three points that the shape may include: Julfar until 1633, Sohar until 1643 ('in 1643 they took the fort at Sohar') and Muscat until 1650 (the Siege of Fort Jesus page: 'since the expulsion of the Portuguese Army from Oman in 1650'). No page opened gives an area for the Ya'rubids. Julfar spec respelled in fx-46 as Ras al Khaymah (UAE) so it resolves; p1620-p1629 patch controls this keyframe.

92,000 km2, 1653-1699: Oman with the Portuguese expelled from Muscat (1650). The page dates no territorial change between 1650 and 1696 except an Omani attack on Mombasa in 1660 that took nothing; unverified in detail: page budget.

121,000 km2 with the Swahili coast from 8.3 S: right for 1700. 'The last Omani attack on December 13 captured the fort' (13 December 1698) and 'the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba fell to the Omani Arabs' (Siege of Fort Jesus page); the shape starts in 1700, two years after the fall.

Same 121,000 km2 for 1718-1740. 'Mombasa would remain in Omani hands until 1728' (Siege of Fort Jesus page), so Mombasa leaves the shape in 1728; the pages opened do not say whether it returned to the Omanis, and the shape keeps the coast to 1743. The civil war of 1718-1724 and the Persian arrival of March 1737 (Ya'rubids page) change no frontier that the pages draw.

union.text: the interior of Oman, held by Sultan bin Murshid and from 1743 by Bal'arab bin Himyar at Nizwa

correction.text: the Swahili coast of the Cliopatria 1741 shape plus the Ya'rubid interior around Nizwa; the coast of Oman is Persian-held from 1742

keyframe_review.note: 28,000 km2, the Swahili coast only (Oman proper is missing from 1741). Ahmad bin Said page (paraphrase): the Persians returned from 1742 to 1744 and controlled much of the country by 1742; the Ya'rubids page (paraphrase): a Persian expedition reached Julfar around October 1742 and the Persians took Muscat in 1743; Sultan bin Murshid was imam in 1742-1743 and Bal'arab bin Himyar, elected again in 1743, held the interior from Nizwa (Bal'arab bin Himyar page). The interior therefore stays Ya'rubid.

correction.text: the interior of Oman, held by Bal'arab bin Himyar from Nizwa until his defeat near Jebel Akhdar in 1749

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (1744-1749). Cliopatria ends the Ya'rubids in 1743 and gives Oman and the Swahili coast to the Sultanate of Oman from 1744, but 'in 1744 he [Ahmad bin Said] was elected Imam' while Bal'arab bin Himyar, chosen imam again in 1743, held the interior; 'in 1749 Ahmad gathered an army and moved against Bal'arab, who was encamped near Jebel Akhdar', and 'in the final battle, in the second half of 1749, Bal'arab was defeated and killed'. The two states overlap here by design; the Persian garrison held the coast until 1747 (Ahmad bin Said page).

region.text: Nizwa, the capital of Nasir bin Murshid

ledger.note: 1624: Nasir bin Murshid founds the Ya'rubid imamate of Oman at Nizwa. The page: the Ya'rubids 'were rulers of Oman between 1624 and 1742' and Nasir moved the capital to Nizwa, the former Ibadhi Imamate capital (paraphrase). The extent of his rule is not on the page.

1633: Nasir bin Murshid expels the Portuguese from Julfar. The page has Nasir's forces expel the Portuguese from Julfar in 1633 (paraphrase). Cliopatria draws the Portuguese holdings of these years as the Iberian Union (to 1639). Region respelled in fx-46 (request R061): the gazetteer cannot resolve 'Julfar', which is the predecessor settlement of Ras al Khaimah ('Julfar (now Ras al-Khaimah)', Ya'rubid dynasty page; Julfar page: 'predecessor settlement to modern Ras Al Khaimah').
1643: the Omanis take the fort at Sohar from the Portuguese. 'In 1643 they took the fort at Sohar.'

region.text: Muscat and the Portuguese holdings in Oman

ledger.note: 1650: the Portuguese are expelled from Oman. The Siege of Fort Jesus page dates the Ya'rubid expansion 'since the expulsion of the Portuguese Army from Oman in 1650'; the Ya'rubids page says Sultan bin Saif captured Muscat without a date and the Omani Empire page puts the end of the Portuguese presence at Muscat in the 'mid-17th century'. Muscat is my reading of 'Oman'.
1696: the Omanis besiege Fort Jesus at Mombasa. The siege ran 'from 13 March 1696 to 13 December 1698'; the Ya'rubids page adds that an earlier attack on Mombasa in 1660 took nothing.

region.text: the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba

ledger.note: 1698: Fort Jesus falls and the Swahili coast with it. 'The last Omani attack on December 13 captured the fort'; 'the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba fell to the Omani Arabs'.
1698: the siege ends on 13 December with the surrender of Fort Jesus.

1728: Mombasa leaves Omani hands. 'Mombasa would remain in Omani hands until 1728.' The page names no taker; the Portuguese are my reading, because the Omani-Portuguese conflicts page gives the war as 'c. 1650 - 1730' between Portugal and the Imamate of Oman.

region.text: the Omani coast, where a Persian force landed

ledger.note: March 1737: a Persian force arrives in Oman. 'A Persian force arrived in March 1737' (Ya'rubids page); it came at the call of Saif bin Sultan II against Bal'arab bin Himyar (Ahmad bin Said page), so the first years are an intervention in the Ya'rubid civil war.

region.text: the coast of Oman, 'much of the country'

ledger.note: 1742: the Persians hold the coast. The page has the Persians returning from 1742 to 1744 and controlling much of the country by 1742 (paraphrase); a Persian expedition reached Julfar around October 1742 (Ya'rubids page). The region is my reading of 'much of the country'. Julfar element respelled in fx-46 (request R094) as Ras al Khaymah, UAE, since the gazetteer cannot resolve 'Julfar' (Julfar is now Ras al-Khaimah). Not changed: the Ya'rubid dynasty page has the October 1742 Persian expedition at Julfar fail to take Sohar or Muscat (Muscat's last forts fell in 1743), so the 1742 date of the loss is the original author's reading.

1743: the Persians take Muscat. The Ya'rubids page has the Persians take Muscat in 1743 (paraphrase); the Bal'arab bin Himyar page: 'In 1743 The Persians took Muscat and again attacked Sohar to the north.'
1743: the Ya'rubid hold on the coast ends with the loss of Muscat; the Persians stay until 1747 (Ahmad bin Said page).

region.text: the Swahili coast of the Cliopatria shape of 1741

ledger.note: 1744: the Swahili coast passes to the Al Bu Said. The pages say only that 'Ahmad bin Sa'id was recognized as Imam only by the governor of Zanzibar' and that his son later governed Mombasa and the East African possessions, both undated; the year is bridged from Cliopatria, which gives the Swahili coast to the Sultanate of Oman from 1744 (confidence 1).

region.text: the interior of Oman, where Bal'arab was encamped near Jebel Akhdar

ledger.note: 1749: Ahmad bin Said defeats Bal'arab. 'In the final battle, in the second half of 1749, Bal'arab was defeated and killed.'
1749: the end of Ya'rubid power. 'This was the end of Yaruba power.' Al Bu Said rule follows (Ahmad bin Said page: 'the first ruler of Oman of the Al Bu Said dynasty').

wars.name: Omani-Portuguese conflicts
wars.outcome: The Portuguese lose their holdings in Oman (1650) and Mombasa (1698); Mombasa leaves Omani hands in 1728. Outcomes are from the Siege of Fort Jesus page; the conflicts page itself gives only the span and the belligerents.
wars.note: Infobox: 'c. 1650 - 1730', Persian Gulf, Indian Ocean and East Africa, Kingdom of Portugal and Imamate of Oman. The page is a stub of an infobox and references.

wars.name: Siege of Fort Jesus (1696-1698)
wars.outcome: Omani victory after 33 months: the fort surrenders on 13 December 1698 and the whole coast of Kenya and Tanzania with Zanzibar and Pemba falls to the Omanis.
wars.note: The Omani Empire page also dates the attack to 1696 under Saif bin Sultan.

wars.name: Ya'rubid civil war (1718-1724)
wars.outcome: A succession dispute after 1718 turns into a civil war in which Muhammad bin Nasir seizes power (1724-1728); no frontier changes on the pages opened.

wars.name: Persian intervention in Oman (1737-1747)
wars.outcome: A Persian force arrives in March 1737 at the call of Saif bin Sultan II; Persian troops return in 1742, take Muscat in 1743 and besiege Sohar; Ahmad bin Said, confirmed governor of Sohar and Barka, is elected imam in 1744 and in 1747 massacres the remaining Persians at Barka (other historians say they left voluntarily).

wars.name: Ahmad bin Said's war against Bal'arab bin Himyar (1749)
wars.outcome: In the second half of 1749 Ahmad's army defeats and kills Bal'arab near Jebel Akhdar: the end of Ya'rubid power.

certainty.note: Tribal interior and coastal forts: no treaty lines; the Portuguese enclaves (Julfar to 1633, Sohar to 1643, Muscat to 1650, Mombasa to 1698) are points, not frontiers.

notes:
Dates of the end disagree: the Ya'rubids page says the dynasty 'ruled Oman between 1624 and 1742', the Omani Empire page gives 1624-1719, Cliopatria ends the row in 1743, and the Ahmad bin Said and Bal'arab bin Himyar pages end 'Yaruba power' in 1749 with Bal'arab's defeat. This dossier follows 1749 and adds two new keyframes (1624-1625 and 1744-1749); the Sultanate of Oman dossier (another group) starts on 20 November 1744, so 1744-1749 is deliberately double-drawn in the interior around Nizwa.

Page budget: 6 pages opened (budget 5); two were thin (Omani-Portuguese conflicts is a stub, Omani Empire gives almost no dates). No page gives an infobox area for the Ya'rubids, so the area check is not done; Cliopatria's 88,000-121,000 km2 is unchecked.

Unsettled: (a) the seat of government 1719-1742 (the pages name only Rustaq, Al-Hazm and Jabrin as residences); (b) what happened to Mombasa after 1728 and who held it (the pages say only 'Omani hands until 1728'); (c) the year the Swahili coast passed to the Al Bu Said (bridged at confidence 1); (d) the 1660 Omani attack on Mombasa (Ya'rubids page) took nothing and has no event; (e) the Cliopatria 1626-1652 shape may already exclude the Portuguese points the keyframe subtracts; (f) the predecessor of the Ya'rubids (the Nabhani rulers) is not on any page opened, so predecessors is empty.
Gazetteer names needed: Julfar (place, Ras al-Khaimah, UAE). Counterparts: the Portuguese holdings are drawn by Cliopatria as iberian-union (to 1639) and kingdom-of-portugal; afsharid-iran and sultanate-of-oman have dossiers.
